facts.statement: PBRT 4e section 11.1 defines the attenuation or extinction coefficient as the sum of the absorption and scattering coefficients.
assumptions: The absorption and scattering coefficients use the same position, direction, wavelength, and distance unit.

facts.statement: PBRT 4e equation 11.5 defines beam transmittance between two points as the exponential of the negative line integral of the attenuation coefficient along the ray.

structuredValue.relationship: T_r(p -> p_prime) = exp(-integral_0^d sigma_t(p + t omega, omega) dt)

assumptions: The ray direction is normalized and d is the distance between the endpoints.

facts.statement: PBRT 4e equation 11.6 states that transmittance is multiplicative across consecutive subsegments of a ray.

structuredValue.relationship: T_r(p -> p_double_prime) = T_r(p -> p_prime) * T_r(p_prime -> p_double_prime)

assumptions: The intermediate point lies on the ray segment between the endpoints.

facts.statement: PBRT 4e equation 11.3 models volume in-scattering through the spherical integral of incident radiance weighted by a phase function and the scattering-to-extinction ratio.

facts.statement: The frozen incident caches use two deterministic full-sphere direction sequences: the local sequence is a half-offset Fibonacci sphere and the distant sequence uses a source-oriented centered-index variant; cache samplers assign every direction equal solid-angle weight 4 pi divided by direction count.

contradictions.currentObservation: The aggregate historical accepted label is broader than the surviving per-fact proof and cannot satisfy production Reference rules.
contradictions.desiredState: Every retained Reference input has one atomic fact with an exact source or independent derivation, explicit configuration status, and a pinned Reference consumer.
contradictions.requiredAction: Do not inherit record 011 acceptance; rebuild the input ledger atomically and resolve or reject every gap.
blockers: Per-value external locators and independent derivations remain incomplete.

contradictions.summary: The Mark I documentation declares reconciliation_mark_i an archive-only renamed root, but its current latest.json and progress.json point to new-lane record 902 under the non-archive reconciliation root.
contradictions.scope: Mark I evidence-root identity and chronology
contradictions.currentObservation: Record-local folders remain evidence, but the two mutable root pointers no longer represent the historical Mark I terminal state.
contradictions.desiredState: An archive manifest identifies Mark I with immutable Git revision/tree and record-local identities while preserving original embedded paths as historical locators.
contradictions.requiredAction: Do not use latest.json or progress.json to establish Mark I identity; reconstruct chronology from immutable Git and record-local evidence.
blockers: The numbered evidence itself contains stale pre-rename paths and does not record the immutable Git commit/tree identity.

contradictions.summary: Several Mark I records use accepted parity or comparison language without pinning the exact CPU Reference revision, complete inputs, and pre-display comparison boundary required for shader-to-Reference conformance.
contradictions.scope: Mark I M3 and M4 shader evidence
contradictions.currentObservation: GPU source hashes, same-scene labels, selected display bytes, GPU-to-GPU quality comparisons, and base-scene prerequisites survive, but none of the cataloged records qualifies as conformance to an exact independently proved CPU Reference.
contradictions.desiredState: Each shader-conformance record freezes the CPU Reference commit and module hashes, serialized physical input/cache packet, GPU source, environment, pre-display quantities, criteria, and tolerance before execution.
contradictions.requiredAction: Retain the records as debug lineage only and build new shader-to-pinned-Reference experiments after the CPU Reference is independently proved.
blockers: No cataloged Mark I shader record pins all required CPU Reference and input identities.

contradictions.summary: Mark I carries both 60000 meter and 100000 meter top/domain values without a final atmosphere-profile ownership decision.
contradictions.scope: Artificial flat atmosphere composition top and finite dome/domain boundary
contradictions.currentObservation: Record 025 uses topAltitudeMeters 100000, while archived POC paths include topAltitudeMeters 60000 and record 040 uses a 60000 meter dome apex alongside topAltitudeMeters 100000.
contradictions.desiredState: Each named target profile independently defines its atmosphere composition top and geometry domain boundary, with explicit ownership and no accidental value conflation.
contradictions.requiredAction: Select, source or classify, and test each boundary before importing the flat/local Reference profile.
blockers: No current target profile decision resolves the competing composition and geometry roles.

contradictions.summary: Mark I uses 9 local-cache directions while its M1 runtime and validation transport packets use 34 and 68 incident directions, without an explicit accepted descriptor mapping or convergence policy.
contradictions.scope: Incident-radiance cache approximation and transport sampling controls
contradictions.currentObservation: The counts coexist as historical implementation choices, and the Mark I audit explicitly says the mismatch needs an explicit cache descriptor policy.
contradictions.desiredState: Cache direction count, transport quadrature count, mapping/interpolation, and error budget are independently defined and validated against no-cache CPU Reference queries.
contradictions.requiredAction: Reconstruct convergence and correspondence for each count and reject any unexplained default mismatch.
blockers: No independent convergence and interpolation study establishes a production descriptor.

contradictions.summary: Mark I computes incidentRadiance from canonicalSolarIrradiance times a dimensionless calibration bridge, while its own later audit requires production local-source brightness to be unit-bearing source radiance or power.
contradictions.scope: Finite local-source radiometry and calibration
contradictions.currentObservation: The historical POC target of unit incident scale is self-calibrated and does not resolve irradiance-to-radiance units, source solid angle, source-path transmittance, or absolute source power.
contradictions.desiredState: A named calibration event provides a unit-bearing target irradiance; apparent solid angle and source-path transmittance are explicit; the CPU Reference solves for fixed spectral source radiance or power and reuses it without per-observer recalibration.
contradictions.requiredAction: Do not promote referenceSpectralIncidentScale as physical source brightness; derive and independently validate a unit-bearing source contract.
blockers: Target source spectrum, calibration event, irradiance, solid angle, transmittance, and uncertainty are unselected.

contradictions.summary: Mark I record 014 reports an earlier distant-cache result, while record 230 changes the lower-boundary source policy to sample and clamp at 2 meters and produces a different selected-ray mean incident delta.
contradictions.scope: Distant incident-radiance cache lower-boundary query policy
contradictions.currentObservation: Both historical records are labeled accepted, but the later boundary realization supersedes the earlier result for reconstruction and neither policy is independently proved as the target rule.
contradictions.desiredState: One explicit lower-boundary contract is derived from accepted geometry/observer inputs and validated against independent no-cache Reference queries, including neighboring cases.
contradictions.requiredAction: Treat record 014 as superseded lineage, retain record 230 as a reconstruction candidate, and run a new target boundary study.
blockers: No independently accepted target lower-boundary query rule exists.

contradictions.summary: The abandoned tree's historical transport-reference label is superseded by the accepted Reference-first policy: a separately pinned target CPU Reference is the implementation authority under physical proof, while the abandoned lane is source-mining material.
contradictions.scope: CPU Reference authority and lineage
contradictions.currentObservation: The old README and fixtures use reference language, but this is a resolved lineage/authority classification rather than a live scientific conflict; source, local policy, and same-lane expectation evidence remain interleaved and require selective mining.
contradictions.desiredState: Keep the accepted authority policy fixed: one exact target CPU Reference revision is proved from external or independent physics, shaders defer to it, and the abandoned lane remains traceable source material rather than a competing oracle.
contradictions.requiredAction: Preserve both historical-label and resolved-policy facts, do not import or bless the abandoned implementation wholesale, and rebuild independent proof around the pinned target CPU Reference.
blockers: The target Reference has not yet been reconstructed or proved from the cataloged facts.

contradictions.summary: The abandoned comparison document names a best current composition stack, while the same evidence set states that no complete matched clear-air bundle or external validation exists.
contradictions.scope: Rayleigh, ozone, aerosol, and profile selection
contradictions.currentObservation: Recorded images and metrics support sensitivity observations and visual preference only; ozone profile/default, matched aerosol validation, absorber coverage, and an independent full-run oracle are absent.
contradictions.desiredState: Each selected composition input is source-backed and the complete case is compared numerically against an independently configured external oracle before becoming a Reference default.
contradictions.requiredAction: Retain the comparison as an experiment to recreate, not as authority for default policy selection.
blockers: No complete source-backed atmosphere bundle or independent full-run comparison is cataloged as reproduced.

contradictions.summary: The Brion table supplies candidate spectral ozone cross sections, while the abandoned comparison keeps an existing 300 DU column/profile that the same documentation says is not source-backed.
contradictions.scope: ozone absorption realization
contradictions.currentObservation: Spectral cross-section provenance is materially stronger than the vertical distribution and column/default provenance, so the combined ozone result cannot inherit the table's authority.
contradictions.desiredState: Cross sections, temperature applicability, column amount, vertical profile, spatial/seasonal scope, and out-of-range policy are each separately sourced and then combined in an independently verified Reference case.
contradictions.requiredAction: Catalog Brion rows as bounded candidate facts but do not promote the 300 DU/profile realization or a full ozone validation result.
blockers: No accepted ozone profile or column policy exists.

contradictions.summary: The abandoned Rayleigh policy contains 48 precise Penndorf/Bruneton samples and a temperature correction, but the exact Penndorf table and immutable Bruneton source revision are not identified.
contradictions.scope: Rayleigh coefficient source lineage
contradictions.currentObservation: Precision of local literals is implementation evidence only; it cannot compensate for absent bibliographic and revision identity.
contradictions.desiredState: Every sample and correction is traced to a precise primary table or immutable upstream source and independently verified before target Reference use.
contradictions.requiredAction: Do not use the 48 values as physics authority until their exact lineage is recovered and checked.
blockers: Exact publication/table and immutable upstream revision are missing.

contradictions.summary: The selected production design requires local incoming directions in a Sun-subpoint radial/tangential/up frame, while the frozen CPU Reference cache stores and samples fixed-frame directions without runtime position-azimuth rotation.
contradictions.scope: Production local-Sun incident-radiance cache coordinate frame and rotational covariance
contradictions.currentObservation: FACT-A32-000218 records an implemented z/rho/fixed-direction cache that omits position azimuth and runtime direction rotation; the selected design-side fact requires a Sun-subpoint local radial/tangential/up direction frame.
contradictions.desiredState: The CPU Reference and selected design must agree on one exact local direction-frame transform, cache-key domain, and rotational-covariance contract with executable tests.
contradictions.requiredAction: Specify and implement the Sun-subpoint frame transform and covariance mapping, or explicitly revise the selected design after an independent symmetry/error review; then test equivalent rotated queries and cache samples across the target domain.
blockers: No exact Sun-subpoint frame equations, runtime azimuth rotation, cache-key update, migration policy, or accepted covariance experiment is present.

contradictions.summary: The retired research, current globe application, shared Sun packet, and abandoned fixture scenarios author 696,340 kilometers, while current and legacy POC globe-state providers author 695,700 kilometers.
contradictions.scope: Current application, shared, fixture, and historical POC solar-radius input convention
contradictions.currentObservation: Two distinct numeric solar-radius values survive across current and historical consumers without an exact source and radius-definition convention pinned to either side.
contradictions.desiredState: One explicitly named solar-radius convention with an exact primary-source locator must own the selected value, with other values retained only as qualified historical inputs.
contradictions.requiredAction: Verify the intended mean, nominal, photospheric, or other radius definition, select its exact value, and update or qualify each consumer.
blockers: Neither local value is linked to a verified exact primary-source claim and radius definition.

observations.statement: The active production requirements require every promoted physics decision, algorithm, numeric value, default, spectral shape, and validation expectation to have a third-party source, source-backed fixture or derivation, or explicitly accepted first-party Algorithm32 evidence; repeated POC behavior is implementation evidence rather than physical authority.

Current code, POC lineage, and fixture repetition do not prove a physical fact.

observations.statement: The documented acceptance chain runs from an independent physical or accepted first-party oracle to the CPU Reference or CPU cache query and only then to a packed GPU query; a shader result can establish conformance to an identified Reference, not physical authority over it.

Agreement with a Reference does not prove that the Reference physics is correct.

observations.nextAction: Use the CPU Reference as the sole implementation oracle and catalog shader work only as downstream conformance.

observations.statement: The production rules explicitly state that an aggregate passing spec count does not establish physical CPU parity or GPU parity; a completion claim must name the exact verification layer executed.
nonClaims: A documented historical count is not a test execution in this catalog.
Contract, shader-source, and fake-renderer tests are not CPU-oracle or GPU physical parity.
observations.nextAction: Classify every test and experiment by the strongest layer it actually executes.

observations.statement: The frozen current-status owner says physical visible Sun, Moon, and star contribution is absent from production; captured celestial meshes and diagnostic stars are presentation only.
nonClaims: Presentation meshes and authored RGB do not implement physical source radiometry.

observations.statement: The selected CelestialContributionCache has no production implementation, runtime result, or parity proof; its physical coordinate reductions, packing, capability limits, and minimal canonical source provider remain unresolved pending qualification.

This fact does not approve any candidate coordinate reduction or GPU layout.

observations.nextAction: Catalog the dossier claims and experiment contracts before recreating the qualification lanes.

observations.statement: Production status classifies record 067 as rolled-back historical execution evidence that does not describe the current tree and cannot accept the selected successor cache.
nonClaims: Cataloging the record-067 experiment contract does not reaccept its result.
Record 067 must not be amended or rerun as the new proof.

observations.nextAction: Use cataloged record 067 only as rejected evidence, then design a new proof after the physical contract is qualified.

observations.statement: The frozen distant incident cache indexes only altitude bin and incoming direction and builds every altitude bin on one observer-up radial line, omitting runtime planet position, local radial frame, and solar-zenith state from the cached field.
nonClaims: Spherical atmosphere symmetry alone does not make a fixed distant-source radiance field invariant to planet position and local horizon orientation.
One toy radial test does not establish a global error bound.
blockers: No independent symmetry derivation or measured error bound justifies reusing the field at all planet positions.
observations.nextAction: Recreate a latitude, solar-zenith, local-frame, horizon, and altitude matrix before accepting any reduced spherical cache domain.

observations.statement: The frozen local incident cache indexes z, rho, and a fixed-frame direction but not position azimuth; it builds at one source-to-observer radial axis and does not rotate the sampled Fibonacci directions for runtime azimuth.
nonClaims: Axial symmetry would require a proved rotation/covariance mapping; simply omitting azimuth does not establish it.
Current tests do not rotate an equivalent query around the source and compare the transformed angular field.
blockers: No rotational-covariance proof or experiment supports the fixed-global-frame lookup.
observations.nextAction: Recreate azimuth-rotation and direction-frame covariance tests across the target local Reference domain.

observations.statement: Although the incident-sampling type describes its cache descriptor as compatibility metadata, the frozen Reference validates only descriptor presence and a callable sampler, and SpectralCalculator ignores the descriptor while consuming samples.
nonClaims: A descriptor existing on a packet does not establish source, geometry, atmosphere, spectral-basis, dimensions, or revision compatibility.
blockers: The CPU oracle can accept an arbitrary operation-ready packet without verifying it belongs to the configured model.
observations.nextAction: Define and test exact Reference-side compatibility invariants before accepting cache-backed oracle results.

observations.statement: The generic cache-build helper forwards both pathIntervalCount and sourceTransmittanceIntervalCount, but the concrete distant and local cache builders consume only pathIntervalCount; source-path sampling remains fixed in the calculator created earlier.
nonClaims: Automatic shader setup may happen to construct both layers from the same execution object; that does not make the standalone request field effective.
blockers: The helper spec uses a spy cache and cannot detect that a concrete builder ignores the request-level source control.
observations.nextAction: Choose one canonical control owner, remove the misleading field or make it effective, and add a real-cache sensitivity test.

observations.statement: The frozen SpectralModel retains ordered wavelengths and exposes an alignment helper, but active Algorithm32 transport obtains only channel count and pairs light-source and atmosphere vectors by array index and length; production does not call SpectralModel.isBasisAligned before Reference evaluation.
nonClaims: Equal vector lengths do not prove equal wavelength samples, ordering, bin widths, or density convention.
The isolated SpectralModel helper spec does not establish that production calls the helper.
blockers: No active Reference boundary proves source and atmosphere spectra share the configured basis identity.
observations.nextAction: Make basis compatibility an enforced operation-boundary invariant and add mismatched-wavelength negative tests.

observations.statement: Canonical channel records contain a 31.333333333333332 nm bin width, but the active SpectralBasis retains only center wavelengths and SpectralValue is an array of bare numbers whose source type permits irradiance or radiance input; density-versus-bin-integral and radiometric units therefore do not survive to Reference transport.
nonClaims: A matching array length does not resolve physical units or angular measure.
This fact does not select density samples or integrated bins; it records that the current contract cannot distinguish them.
blockers: The direct-source packet, transport equations, and spectral basis lack one consistent dimensional convention.
observations.nextAction: Define unit-bearing spectral density or bin-integral packets and rederive every conversion into Reference transport.

observations.statement: The frozen production tests do not run Algorithm32.evaluate end to end with CanonicalAtmosphere, a real geometry, a real source, and an optional real incident cache; facade, Reference, and cache tests use vacuum models, stubs, or isolated arithmetic.
nonClaims: This is a static coverage audit, not a report that the source test lane was executed here.
Individual owner contract tests do not establish integrated Reference physics.
blockers: No accepted selected-ray oracle fixture currently exercises the assembled real production owners.
observations.nextAction: Create source-backed selected-ray fixtures and an end-to-end CPU Reference lane before using it as the shader oracle.

observations.statement: The frozen Algorithm32 facade constructs its default CPU Reference without incident-radiance sampling, while shader setup automatically builds and binds an incident-radiance cache; default facade evaluation is therefore not the same configured scattering path that the automatic shader setup is intended to execute.
nonClaims: This static mismatch does not prove what a GPU draw returns.
Renderer mechanics are outside the claim; the issue is that the proposed Reference oracle and shader model inputs differ.
blockers: No conformance experiment can be interpreted until Reference and shader evaluate the same incident-radiance configuration.
observations.nextAction: Make the facade expose or build the exact Reference sampling state used by shader setup, then rerun pre-display parity.

observations.statement: The frozen modified flat and flat32 consumer code imports physical spectral-density factories that do not exist in the production tree and passes spectralIrradianceDensity to DistantSunLightSource, whose constructor requires spectralChannels; those consumer paths cannot currently construct the documented production source packet.
nonClaims: The missing files are not proof that the proposed spectral-density contract is physically correct.
This fact records frozen workspace consistency, not an executed build result.
blockers: The intended unit-bearing physical source packet is absent and the active constructor contract is different.
observations.nextAction: Catalog the intended packet design and source data, then choose and implement one physically explicit constructor contract before porting either app.

observations.statement: When a spherical source path has no explicit endDistanceMeters, the frozen Reference returns a ground-blocked path for any forward ground intersection before it applies sourcePathLimit.maxDistanceMeters; it therefore also blocks an inward finite source whose distance cap lies before the ground hit.
nonClaims: The audited test does not cover an inward ray whose finite source lies closer than the ground.
This finding does not challenge ground blocking when the ground is the nearest physical boundary.
blockers: The Reference does not compare the finite source distance with the ground-intersection distance before declaring the source path blocked.
observations.nextAction: Order the ground and finite-source boundaries by distance and add a selected-ray case with the source cap before ground.

observations.statement: The frozen FlatEarthGeometry resolves local incident-cache access by independently searching every configured z and rho bin for minimum absolute distance; exact ties retain the earliest array entry, non-finite coordinates select index zero with a diagnostic, and no interpolation is performed.
nonClaims: The first and last entries are used for an out-of-range diagnostic, but an unsorted array is still searched globally and is not clamped to an endpoint.
Nearest-bin selection is implementation behavior, not evidence that its reconstruction error is physically acceptable.
blockers: No source-backed error bound or reconstructed experiment establishes nearest-bin access as sufficient for the retained local-cache domains.
observations.nextAction: Pin ordered cache domains and compare nearest-bin Reference results with an independently evaluated interpolation or direct-transport oracle.

observations.statement: During frozen distant and local incident-cache generation, a null geometry build ray is stored as an all-zero spectral vector for that coordinate; runtime sampling subsequently emits that zero vector with the ordinary directional quadrature weight.
nonClaims: A stored zero does not preserve whether it arose from ground blocking or from a computed zero-radiance path.
The audited local-cache spec does not directly assert its identical null-ray branch.
observations.nextAction: Retain the zero-contribution Reference rule only with selected blocked-ray fixtures and explicit blocked-value provenance where diagnostics require it.

observations.statement: The frozen distant cache throws for invalid coordinates or missing generated values, while the local cache records a diagnostic and returns an empty sample array; SpectralCalculator converts that local empty result into zero incident in-scattering, contrary to the production requirement that missing or invalid cache samples fail loudly.
nonClaims: A diagnostic retained in memory is not a loud failure at the CPU Reference operation boundary.
The zero fallback can conceal stale or incomplete cache state as a physically dark contribution.
blockers: The two cache kinds do not implement one authoritative failure contract, and the local behavior violates the current production requirement.
observations.nextAction: Make local invalid and missing access fail at the Reference boundary, align both cache kinds, and add negative end-to-end tests.

observations.statement: The frozen spherical Reference maps runtime distant-cache access by clamping altitude to cacheBoundaryAltitudeMeters, normalizing by atmosphere height, and flooring into a cache bin; cache generation samples bin zero at the clamped boundary altitude and every later bin at its uniform altitude-bin center.
nonClaims: The arithmetic and toy tests do not establish a physical error bound for the bin count, boundary altitude, or sample locations.
This CPU fact does not establish shader conformance for linear interpolation.
blockers: The altitude discretization and special first-bin sample require independent convergence and boundary-bias evidence.
observations.nextAction: Recreate altitude-domain convergence against direct CPU transport before accepting the cache mapping.

observations.statement: SphericalEarthGeometry and DistantSunIncidentRadianceCache each retain their own radii, altitude-bin count, and boundary-altitude facts, while DistantSunLightSource combines request-supplied radii and boundary overrides with source-owned cache dimensions; no frozen operation boundary enforces that the geometry runtime mapping and generated cache use identical domain facts.
nonClaims: Callers can manually provide matching values, but the current Reference boundary does not prove or enforce that match.
A structurally valid cache descriptor is not evidence that it matches the active geometry domain.
blockers: A cache can be built under domain facts different from those used to resolve runtime altitude keys.
observations.nextAction: Create one canonical distant-cache domain descriptor, require exact geometry/cache compatibility, and add mismatched-domain negative tests.

observations.statement: FlatEarthGeometry owns the z/rho arrays used to resolve runtime cache access, while LocalSunLightSource independently owns the z/rho arrays copied into the generated local cache; SharedModel aggregation and Algorithm32 shape checks do not compare the two grids.
nonClaims: Separate arrays can be manually configured with equal values; the defect is that equality and ownership are not enforced.
Matching array lengths alone would not establish matching bin coordinates.
blockers: Runtime keys can address a cache generated from a different physical z/rho grid.
observations.nextAction: Move spatial grid authority to one geometry descriptor and reject every cache whose exact grid identity differs from it.

observations.statement: The frozen distant and local cache builders copy calculator.computeRadiance(...).inScattered directly into generated cache values without checking spectral length, finiteness, units, or basis identity; later Reference scattering indexes those arrays by the active channel count and can propagate undefined or non-finite values.
nonClaims: The calculator's current output may usually match its own basis; the cache operation boundary does not enforce that invariant.
Successful float packing would not prove the radiometric measure or wavelength identity of the values.
blockers: Malformed, stale, or mismatched spectra can enter the CPU oracle and any derived shader payload without a loud failure.
observations.nextAction: Validate every generated vector against an exact unit-bearing spectral-basis descriptor before storing or packing it, with negative tests for length and non-finite values.

observations.statement: The frozen LocalSunLightSource accepts radiusMeters equal to zero; if a path sample lies exactly at that zero-radius source center, FlatEarthGeometry supplies a fallback upward direction but direct-light falloff divides the positive reference distance by a zero safe distance and produces unbounded spectral values.
nonClaims: A zero-radius source may be a useful point-source abstraction, but its radiometric normalization and singularity treatment are not defined here.
The fallback direction prevents a zero-vector normalization error; it does not make the radiance finite.
blockers: The Reference permits a finite constructor configuration that can generate infinite incident radiance.
observations.nextAction: Either forbid zero radius for this finite-source owner or define a separately normalized point-source contract with a finite evaluated domain.

observations.statement: CanonicalAtmosphere enforces positive scale heights but only finiteness for the Rayleigh coefficient scale, Mie Angstrom parameters, single-scattering albedo, and phase asymmetry g; negative optical coefficients, albedo outside zero to one, and an invalid g magnitude can therefore enter Reference transport.
nonClaims: The catalog has not yet sourced exact accepted domains for every retained atmosphere parameterization.
Finiteness is a numeric shape check, not a physical-domain proof.
blockers: The CPU Reference can be configured with values that yield negative or undefined physical medium behavior.
observations.nextAction: Source each parameter domain, enforce it at construction, and add negative configuration tests before accepting CanonicalAtmosphere as an oracle.

observations.statement: Both frozen light-source owners require each solarIrradiance value to be finite but do not require it to be non-negative; the distant source copies negative values directly into incidentRadiance and the local source scales them into Reference transport.
nonClaims: This fact does not resolve the separate irradiance-versus-radiance dimensional ambiguity.
Signed intermediate residuals in a numerical method do not justify accepting negative physical source input.
blockers: The Reference accepts a physically invalid direct-source spectrum without a loud configuration failure.
observations.nextAction: Require a unit-bearing non-negative source spectrum and add negative-value rejection tests at the source and assembled Reference boundaries.

observations.statement: The frozen CPU Reference distant-cache sampler consumes one integer altitude-bin index and returns that exact bin, while the optional shader linear-altitude-v1 path computes a fractional bin coordinate and interpolates packed altitude samples; no CPU Reference path implements that interpolation policy for downstream shader conformance.
nonClaims: Static shader source does not establish an executed GPU result.
This is not a shader-conformance fact: under the fixed authority direction, the shader must defer to an exact CPU Reference policy that is absent for linear lookup.
blockers: There is no same-policy CPU oracle, pinned Reference revision and input set, or experiment-backed pre-display comparison for linear altitude lookup.
observations.nextAction: Define linear reconstruction in the CPU Reference or remove the shader-only mode, then run packed pre-display conformance against that pinned Reference.

observations.statement: The frozen flat geometry, local source, and local cache accept any non-empty finite z/rho arrays without enforcing ascending order or unique coordinates; runtime nearest-bin search still scans every entry, while its out-of-range diagnostic assumes the first and last entries describe the range.
nonClaims: Unsorted bins do not force endpoint clamping because the implementation searches every entry for the nearest value.
Duplicate coordinates make tie ownership depend on array order and can leave distinct cache indices for the same physical coordinate.
blockers: The Reference has no canonical bin-domain invariant or negative coverage for unsorted and duplicate grids.
observations.nextAction: Require strictly increasing unique grids under one domain owner and add construction and runtime mapping tests for rejected invalid arrays.
